scripts.//order: Inter-package imports resolve via `exports`/`types` that point at the gitignored `./dist/index.*` outputs. npm runs `-ws` scripts in path order, which does NOT match the dependency graph — without an explicit chain the downstream packages' tsc/vitest fail with TS2307 in a fresh checkout. Pre-build the chain: codec → client + dom → app.
scripts.prebuild-chain: npm -w @ciri/codec run build && npm -w @ciri/client run build && npm -w @ciri/dom run build && npm -w @ciri/app run build
scripts.test: npm run prebuild-chain && npm -ws --if-present run test
scripts.build: npm run prebuild-chain && npm -ws --if-present run build
scripts.typecheck: npm run prebuild-chain && npm -ws --if-present run typecheck
scripts.//dev: Starts the dev bridge (ws ↔ ciri-server TCP), the vite demo server, AND a `tsc --watch` per upstream package so source edits in `@ciri/codec` / `client` / `dom` / `app` rebuild their `dist/` automatically; without those watchers, vite serves the stale dist forever — symptom is 'my code change is in source but the browser shows the old behavior' (every time). `prebuild-chain` runs once up front so the very first dev server start has fresh dist before vite resolves it. Requires `ciri-server` to be running separately with `[remote] enabled = true`. Bridge defaults to TCP 7899 (not ciri-server's protocol default 7890, which collides with Clash on Windows); set your ciri config's [remote] port to match or pass `--tcp-port` to dev:bridge. See README.md.
scripts.//dev:watch-flags: `--preserveWatchOutput` keeps each watcher's banner around in the concurrent log instead of clearing it. `--pretty false` strips colors so concurrently's per-process prefix isn't mangled.
scripts.dev: npm run prebuild-chain && concurrently --kill-others-on-fail --names codec,client,dom,app,bridge,demo --prefix-colors gray,cyan,magenta,yellow,blue,green "npm -w @ciri/codec exec -- tsc -p tsconfig.json --watch --preserveWatchOutput --pretty false" "npm -w @ciri/client exec -- tsc -p tsconfig.json --watch --preserveWatchOutput --pretty false" "npm -w @ciri/dom exec -- tsc -p tsconfig.json --watch --preserveWatchOutput --pretty false" "npm -w @ciri/app exec -- tsc -p tsconfig.json --watch --preserveWatchOutput --pretty false" "npm -w @ciri/bridge run start" "npm -w @ciri/demo run dev"
scripts.//dev:bridge: Direct `node` (not nested `npm -w … run start`) so `npm run dev:bridge -- --tcp-port 7900` actually forwards the flag — npm consumes args after `--` for the directly-invoked script, but a wrapping `npm run start` swallows them as npm config instead of passing them on. Pre-builds the upstream packages first because bridge imports `decodeClientHello` from `@ciri/client`, which resolves through its gitignored `dist/`.
scripts.prebuild-bridge: npm -w @ciri/codec run build && npm -w @ciri/client run build
